summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of stroke, tracheostomy, GJ tube, atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation, diabetes, and recurrent infections was admitted for a clogged GJ tube, urinary tract infection, and tracheostomy leak. He developed hypoxia during transport due to a mucus plug, which resolved with suctioning. He was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics—cefepime and daptomycin—due to a history of resistant organisms, despite contaminated urine culture. The tracheostomy was successfully exchanged, and the GJ tube was unclogged using a 5 cc syringe and diet coke. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic completion. His infection resolved, leg pain was managed with increased gabapentin, fentanyl patch, and capsaicin cream, and he was discharged to extended care with follow-up plans for INR monitoring and CK checks.
